speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing your history. To better understand your condition, can you describe the specific sensations you experience during your episodes of dizziness and vertigo?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Do these episodes of spinning last only a few seconds to minutes, or do they persist for hours? Also, have you noticed any ringing in your ears (tinnitus) or hearing loss in one specific ear?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). Given the classic presentation of brief, position-dependent vertigo without auditory symptoms, I am confident in this diagnosis. I will now request images to confirm the absence of other pathology and guide our next steps. REQUEST IMAGES: Inner_Ear_Canal
